title: Modules
subtitle: CommonJS require/exports, ES Modules import/export, and Node's module resolution
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Large programs need to be split into reusable files. Without a module system, every variable is global and files have no way to declare what they export or import.
whyItExists.solution: Node.js supports two module systems: CommonJS (require/module.exports — the original, synchronous) and ES Modules (import/export — the standard, supports async loading). You can use either; the choice affects syntax and some behaviors.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Every Node.js project uses modules. Use ES Modules for new projects. Use CommonJS when working with older codebases, legacy npm packages, or config files that require it (like .cjs).
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: N/A — modules are fundamental to Node.js.

explainModes.beginner: Node.js programs are split into multiple files called modules. Each file can export things (functions, objects, values) and other files can import them. CommonJS uses require() and module.exports. ES Modules use import and export. They're two different ways to do the same thing.
explainModes.simple: CommonJS (default, .js with no type:module): const fs = require('fs'); module.exports = { myFn }; exports.name = 'Alice'. ES Modules (.mjs or type:module in package.json): import { readFile } from 'fs/promises'; export function myFn() {}; export default class App {}. require() is synchronous. import is async (supports top-level await). Built-in modules: 'fs', 'path', 'os', 'http', 'events', 'crypto', 'stream', etc. Prefix with node: for clarity: require('node:fs').
explainModes.standard: Module resolution order for require('module'): (1) Built-in module (fs, path)? Return it. (2) Starts with ./ or /? Load that file. (3) Look in node_modules/. Try index.js and package.json 'main'. Circular requires: allowed in CommonJS — the partial export at the time of the circular require is returned. Avoid circular imports in practice. Caching: require() caches modules — calling require() twice on the same file returns the same export object (singleton).
explainModes.technical: ES Module internals: import statements are hoisted and parsed before execution (static linking). This enables tree-shaking by bundlers (dead code elimination). Dynamic import: import('./module.js') — returns a Promise, works anywhere (even CommonJS). Interoperability: you can import a CJS module from ESM. You cannot require() an ESM module — use dynamic import() instead. `__dirname` and `__filename` don't exist in ESM — use import.meta.url and fileURLToPath instead.
explainModes.deepDive: The dual module hazard: a package can expose both CJS and ESM via the 'exports' field in package.json. If someone imports with both systems in the same process, two instances of the module exist (breaking singletons). Package authors solve this by preferring one or using the 'exports' conditional carefully. Top-level await (ESM only): you can await at the top level of a module — useful for async initialization. This causes any importing module to await that module's evaluation.

questions.question: What is the key difference between `require()` (CommonJS) and `import` (ES Modules)?
options: require() is faster; import is slower
require() is synchronous and dynamic (can be inside if/functions); import is static (hoisted, parsed before execution) and enables tree-shaking
import only works with npm packages; require() works with built-in modules
They are interchangeable — just different syntax for the same behavior
questions.explanation: require() is synchronous — it reads and evaluates the module file immediately when called, and can appear anywhere in the code (inside conditions, functions). import is static — it's parsed before the module executes, which lets bundlers know exactly what's imported at build time (tree-shaking: unused exports can be eliminated). For dynamic loading in ESM, use import() (the dynamic import function) which returns a Promise.

faq.q: How do I switch a Node.js project to ES Modules?
faq.a: Add `"type": "module"` to your package.json. Then rename .js files to .mjs, or leave them as .js (the type field makes all .js files ESM). Change require() to import and module.exports to export. Replace __dirname and __filename with: `const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`.

examples: const express = require('express') — CJS import of Express
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client' — ESM import of Prisma ORM
export default router — Express router exported as default
